vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: dynamic-temperature
Version: 1.0.1

The skill bundle contains only documentation and guidelines for selecting LLM temperature settings based on task types (e.g., 0.0 for irreversible actions, 0.8 for creative writing). There is no executable code, no network activity, and no instructions that would lead to data exfiltration or unauthorized access. The files SKILL.md and DEPRECATED.md are purely informational and align with the stated purpose of the skill.

llm.summary: The skill is an instruction-only guideline for picking LLM temperature values and does not request credentials, install software, or perform unexpected actions — it is internally coherent with minor documentation inconsistencies.

dimensions.detail: Name, description, and instructions align: the skill only provides rules for selecting temperatures. It does not request unrelated credentials or binaries. Minor documentation inconsistency: the Per‑Skill Recommendations list includes temperatures (0.1, 0.4) not shown in the main Temperature Scale table, but this is a small editorial mismatch rather than a security issue.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: SKILL.md only instructs the agent to classify tasks and use the recommended temperature and suggests setting model defaults or passing temperature to subagents. It does not instruct reading arbitrary files, sending data externally, or accessing credentials. Note: the Implementation Notes recommend changing agents.defaults.models (a global config) which, if followed, affects broader agent behavior — this is a behavioral/design decision rather than a malicious action.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec and no code files — instruction-only skill. Nothing is written to disk or downloaded at install time.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill requires no environment variables, credentials, or config paths. It only advises updating existing agent configuration values — there are no disproportionate secret or credential requests.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: Skill is not always-enabled and does not claim elevated privileges or make persistent system changes. The DEPRECATED.md notes that temperature rules might belong in SOUL.md (a global identity file) — moving rules there would create broader, persistent behavioral changes; the current skill itself does not do that.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill is low-risk: it only documents how to pick an LLM temperature and requires no installs or secrets. Before using: (1) review and, if desired, standardize the small temperature inconsistencies (e.g., 0.1 and 0.4 appear in per-skill suggestions but not the main table); (2) test the rules in a non-production agent to ensure the classification rules (irreversible vs. creative) match your workflow; (3) be cautious about actually applying changes to agents.defaults.models or moving the rules into SOUL.md — doing so makes the behavior global and affects every interaction. If you want this behavior applied automatically across all interactions, understand that placing it in a global identity file (SOUL.md) is a deliberate design choice with broader impact.
